clue.text: Where the 17 takes his money?

parts.note: a crocodilian banks its cash in the island tax haven that shares its name

explanation.surface: A question about where a reptile might stash its savings.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is CROCODILE. A cayman is a South American relative of the crocodile, and the Cayman Islands are a well-known Caribbean tax haven.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cayman Islands are an offshore banking haven, and the caiman is a crocodilian reptile.

clue.text: Priest keeps out fashionable business

indicators.note: the priest keeps the other word held inside him

parts.note: a curé is a French parish priest
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clergyman keeps away from the fashion trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like part of 'keeps out' but is the letters held inside CURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Couture is the design and making of high fashion clothes as a trade.

clue.text: Solver no good? Won't be so forever

parts.note: the solver is addressed as you

explanation.surface: A remark that the solver is no use and will change one day.
explanation.definitionFit: Youth is temporary: being youthful is a state nobody keeps for ever.

clue.text: Suffer headless flier to flap

parts.note: to ail is to suffer or be unwell

indicators.note: headless means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: a heron is a bird, a flier

explanation.surface: An ill bird that has lost its head flaps about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headless' cuts HERON to ERON.
explanation.definitionFit: An aileron is a hinged flap on an aircraft's wing used to control roll.

clue.text: 15 made of 25, 26 and 27

indicators.note: the cat is said to be made of these metals, so their symbols are mixed into a new arrangement

parts.note: 25 is GOLD, and or is the heraldic word for gold
26 is SILVER, whose chemical symbol is Ag
27 is COPPER, whose chemical symbol is Cu

explanation.surface: A cat that is apparently cast from three metals.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 is PUMA. The three metal answers 25, 26 and 27 give OR (heraldic gold), AG and CU; 'made of' mixes ORAGCU into the cat's other name.
explanation.definitionFit: The puma and the cougar are the same big American cat, known also as the mountain lion.

clue.text: Song people don't listen to any more means expense

parts.words: people don't listen to any more
parts.note: something no longer in fashion is out
a lay is a song or ballad

explanation.surface: An old song nobody bothers with now costs money.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlay is money spent on something.

clue.text: Spooner's fodder put through the mill for dog

indicators.note: Spooner's means the opening sounds of two words are swapped

parts.note: hay is animal fodder
milled grain is ground

explanation.surface: Feed for animals is milled into dog food.
explanation.walkthrough: HAY GROUND with the first sounds swapped gives GRAY HOUND, entered as GREYHOUND.
explanation.definitionFit: A greyhound is a slender fast breed of racing dog.

clue.text: Cage bird rebelled and upset everything

parts.note: rose as in rose up against rulers

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A caged bird rebelled and overturned everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ALL to LLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosella is a brightly coloured Australian parakeet often kept as a pet.

clue.text: It's from 2 onwards, scrambled eggs (pair) with scone

indicators.note: like scrambled eggs, the letters are mixed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A breakfast of a pair of scrambled eggs and a scone.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 is YOUNG: what happens from youth onwards. 'scrambled' mixes EGGS, PAIR and SCONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting older is a process that runs from youth onwards.

clue.text: Outstanding repeat for singer

definitions.meaning: an informal noun for something remarkable or excellent, a real humdinger
the Scottish pop singer of the 1960s, famous for Shout

explanation.walkthrough: 'repeat' points to the shape of the word, one syllable said twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A remarkable example is informally called this, and it is also the stage name of a Scottish pop star.

clue.text: Literary entertainment for the day (8 May) the girls wandered round

indicators.note: the scrambled girls are placed round the day, enclosing it
the girls wandering about means their letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: 8 May 1945 was VE Day, Victory in Europe

explanation.surface: A diversion for a holiday on 8 May, when the girls strolled about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandered' shuffles THE GIRLS into LIGHTRSE, and 'round' puts that around VE, the letters for Victory in Europe Day.
explanation.definitionFit: Light verse is humorous or whimsical poetry, written to amuse rather than to move.

clue.text: The 17 that takes your money?

definitions.meaning: a broad-snouted marsh crocodile of the Indian subcontinent bears this name
a street robber who attacks people and grabs their cash

explanation.walkthrough: 17 is CROCODILE; the Indian marsh crocodile is called the mugger.
explanation.definitionFit: The marsh crocodile of India is so named, and a street thief who robs with violence is also called that.

clue.text: Later to be followed by 17

definitions.meaning: at some point soon in the future
the playground rhyme 'See you later, alligator' gets the reply ending in 'crocodile'

explanation.walkthrough: 17 is CROCODILE: the rhyme goes 'See you later, alligator / In a while, crocodile'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means after a short time, and it is the line that ends with crocodile in the old rhyme.

clue.text: Part of book including queen with prince as character

indicators.note: the page of the book holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a page is one leaf of a book
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual queen
a prince is a king's son

explanation.surface: A section of a book with a queen and a prince in its cast.
explanation.definitionFit: A personage is a person of note, as a character in a story or play may be.

clue.text: Second wave hits little room that has reproductive function

parts.note: a perm is a hair wave
a cell is a small room

explanation.surface: Another wave of attack hits a small chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: A sperm cell is the male gamete, whose job is fertilisation.

clue.text: Cat where it sat (say) on the mat (nearly)

indicators.note: say signals that the seat is given by its sound only

parts.note: a pew is a church bench, where one sits

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A twist on the nursery line 'The cat sat on the mat'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns PEW into PU by sound, and 'nearly' cuts MAT to MA; 'on' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: The puma is a large wild American feline, also called the mountain lion.

clue.text: Row in drawer?

definitions.meaning: a line of seats or one layer in a stack
someone who draws a game, i.e. ties it, is jokingly one who ties

explanation.walkthrough: A drawn match is a tie, so a 'drawer' is whimsically one who ties.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one of a series of rows or levels, and jokingly one who ties a match.

clue.text: 8 sees 26 among the 25 that may be trashed

indicators.note: may be signals the word can be turned into something else by rearranging

explanation.surface: Ageing brings grey among the blond, something that may be thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is AGEING PROCESS, 26 SILVER, 25 GOLD: the old song 'Silver Threads Among the Gold'. 'may be' rearranges TRASHED.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey hairs among blonde ones are the silver strands of the old song's title.

clue.text: Walking girls pretending to cry?

definitions.meaning: a line of schoolchildren walking two by two is named after a long reptile
insincere weeping is called by the name of this reptile's tears

explanation.walkthrough: A crocodile is a line of schoolchildren walking in pairs; crocodile tears are false grief.
explanation.definitionFit: Schoolchildren walking in pairs form this file, and fake tears are named after the reptile.

clue.text: Monastic mountain society found among gamblers?

indicators.note: the society is found among the gamblers, inside their venue

parts.note: a casino is where gamblers gather

explanation.surface: A religious community discovered in a gambling crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: Monte Cassino is the Italian mountain with a famous Benedictine abbey.
explanation.definitionFit: Monte Cassino is the hill in Italy topped by the abbey founded by St Benedict.

clue.text: Pupil (of the eye) is compartmentalised

parts.note: L for learner, a pupil
ocular means of the eye

explanation.surface: A remark about the pupil of the eye being divided up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pupil' suggests the eye, but here it is a learner, L.
explanation.definitionFit: Locular means divided into small cavities or compartments, as in botany.

clue.text: Spectator leader supplied energy in tablet

indicators.note: the energy goes inside the stone tablet

parts.note: a stele is an upright inscribed stone slab
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A magazine editor took an energy pill.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Steele co-founded The Spectator with Joseph Addison in 1711.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Steele was co-founder and a leading writer of the early Spectator periodical.

clue.text: Making play with small Scotch and loud Greek

parts.note: a dram is a small measure of whisky

indicators.note: loud means the Greek dialect word is taken as heard rather than as spelt

parts.note: Attic is the Greek of ancient Athens

explanation.surface: A man downs a little whisky and a noisy Greek joins in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loud' gives ATTIC as heard, with a single T.
explanation.definitionFit: Something theatrical, made into a play or with a sense of drama, is described this way.

clue.text: The Sun, champion of comfort

parts.note: Sol is the Latin name of the sun
an ace is an expert or champion

explanation.surface: A tabloid newspaper hailed as the champion of comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun looks like the British tabloid but is the star, SOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Solace is consolation or relief offered in distress.

clue.text: Help, say, in bloomer, in short

indicators.note: the example abbreviation goes inside the trimmed flower
the flower is cut short by losing the letters of in

parts.note: a lupin is a flowering plant, a bloomer
say means for example, EG

explanation.surface: A request for assistance with something in one's knickers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests the old-fashioned underwear, but it is a flowering plant; 'in short' is read as 'minus in', and the first 'in' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg up is a boost or bit of help in getting started.

clue.text: Premier pianist indulging in weird speak

indicators.note: indulging in weird speak suggests garbled talk, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A head of government who plays the piano and speaks in odd ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indulging in' signals the anagram of WEIRD SPEAK.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignacy Paderewski was a celebrated Polish concert pianist who became Prime Minister of Poland in 1919.

clue.text: First virtuous, then venerable …

definitions.meaning: first place in a contest wins the top medal
someone very good is 'as good as' this metal

explanation.walkthrough: 'then venerable' begins the run of metals that continues into 26 and 27.
explanation.definitionFit: First place earns the top medal, and a well-behaved person is called good as this metal.

clue.text: … then pirate …

parts.note: the run of metals continues with the surname of Long John, the pirate of Treasure Island

explanation.walkthrough: After gold, the second medal metal, which is also the name of Treasure Island's one-legged pirate; 'venerable' at the end of 25's clue hints at silver hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Long John Silver is the famous pirate in Stevenson's novel Treasure Island.

clue.text: … then policeman

parts.note: the run of metals ends with the slang word for a police officer

explanation.walkthrough: The sequence gold, silver, then a third metal that is also slang for a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is British slang for a police officer, as well as the third medal metal.
